conviction_note: Near-flat and deliberately so: every bearish item I could find is already in the wire (the RMB5.30bn SAMR penalty of 2026-07-25 and its Q2 booking, the +3%-8% Q2 guide, the take-rate risk from the exclusivity/MFN remedies, the 8% consensus EPS cut, the 50% de-rate to a fresh 52-week low), so the only residual is a factual correction — the 'first summer traffic decline since 2022' projection that has been attached to Chinese travel names since 31 Aug is contradicted by CAAC's own July print (+3.9%) and by the Big-3's H1 revenue (+9.7% to +11.1%) — offset by genuine hotel ADR deflation. Sum of findings is +0.5 against a 6.54% option-implied move, i.e. I have close to nothing here and say so. Note separately for the record that the baseline's history is not entirely unusable: I could confirm two of its eight rows ARE real earnings reactions (2026-02-25 amc Q4 print -> 2026-02-26 -2.59%; 2026-06-24 amc Q1 print -> 2026-06-25 -12.55%), and the clean one was ~2x the then-implied move — that argues the 6.54% straddle may understate the tail but says nothing about sign, so it is not filed as a finding.

findings.finding: The bearish Chinese-travel datapoint circulating since 2026-08-31 — Flight Master's projection that Chinese carriers' July+August traffic would fall 3.6% y/y to 142m, 'the first contraction in the peak season since 2022' — is contradicted by CAAC's actual July 2026 print published ten days earlier: 74.63m passenger trips, +3.9% y/y, domestic +4.1%, international +2.3%; and forward bookings measured by 2026-09-08 for the unusual 13-day 25 Sep-7 Oct holiday window show 6.06m domestic air tickets (+~14% y/y) and 2.07m international/cross-border (+~7% y/y), with multi-destination trips +25% y/y.
findings.why_not_priced: The projection, not the print, is what got syndicated: the -3.6% figure ran in the 2026-08-31 wire story about the Big Three's H1 losses and has been the frame for Chinese travel demand ever since, while the CAAC volume release got a Xinhua paragraph and no equity coverage. If the market held the volume picture (air volumes +3.9% in July, Big-3 H1 revenue +9.7%/+11.1%/+10.5% — a cost/fuel problem, not a demand problem) plus double-digit forward holiday ticket growth measured a week ago, TCOM would not be printing a fresh 52-week low on the day of the print (spot 39.535, only 2.16% above the 52-week low) and the 25-delta skew would be negative with calls bid rather than +0.61 vol points with put/call OI at 0.90. All of this post-dates the company's last guidance of 2026-06-24, so none of it is in the +3%-8% Q2 guide the sell side is marking to.
findings.independence: The same Big-3 H1 results that carried the -3.6% projection also disclose revenue growth of +10.5%/+11.1%/+9.7% with losses driven by a 35-38% fuel cost increase — a different fact in the same document that cuts the opposite way to its own headline: https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2026/08/31/china039s-three-biggest-airlines-post-heavy-first-half-losses-as-fuel-shock-bites . Separately and from a different source, the 25 Sep-7 Oct booking data (Qunar, a Trip.com Group subsidiary, and Umetrip): https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/09/11/chinas-13-day-holiday-hack-sends-travel-bookings-up-119/ (2026-09-11).

findings.finding: China industry hotel RevPAR fell ~6% y/y in July 2026 (occupancy -3pp, ADR -1%) and Hilton cut its full-year China RevPAR outlook from roughly flat to a low-single-digit decline — a rate/ADR deflation that lands on Trip.com's highest-take-rate line, accommodation reservation (RMB6.5bn and +17% y/y in Q1 2026), and that post-dates the 2026-06-24 guidance, so tonight's Q3 outlook is the first management commentary to incorporate it.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced and I am sizing it as such — this got a CNBC story and a Goldman note, so it is nearer wire copy than edge. What is not priced is the interaction: OTA accommodation revenue is commission on room-nights x ADR, so a market reading 'Chinese travel volumes are fine' off holiday booking counts is reading the wrong variable, and a Q3 revenue guide at or below the Q2 +3%-8% band is the single most likely thing to move this name — the last guide-down, on 2026-06-24, produced a -12.55% next-day reaction. If this were fully in the price the 25-delta skew would be materially positive rather than +0.61 vol points.
findings.independence: Tongcheng Travel's own Q2 2026 print (2026-08-26/31, a different company reporting the same market) shows the split: accommodation revenue +11.1% in 1H on ADR growth and a mix shift to 3-star-and-above, while transportation ticketing fell 2.3% — https://www.prnewswire.com/apac/news-releases/tongcheng-travels-revenue-reaches-rmb9-992-8-million-in-1h2026--302858196.html . Note this cuts partly AGAINST my own finding on ADR, which is why the band is wide and the size small.

searched_and_found_nothing: Whether the RMB5.301bn SAMR penalty (RMB3,521m fine + RMB1,658m confiscation + RMB122m deposit refund, decision 2026-07-25, 6-K filed 2026-07-27) would be a surprise as to accounting period — it is not: no provision was taken in Q1 (company said it could not estimate losses), but that it lands in the June quarter is already in published previews, e.g. the Seeking Alpha Q2 preview of 2026-09-13 and Bamboo Works. Wire copy. Dropped.

Take-rate/market-share damage from the SAMR remedies (cessation of exclusive cooperation, abolition of 'all-network lowest price', removal of automated pricing tools) — thoroughly covered in the 2026-07-27 fine coverage and named explicitly in the 2026-09-13 preview. Priced.

A new or enlarged buyback as an offsetting announcement — the US$5bn authorisation dates to Aug 2025 and ~US$916m was executed by late April 2026, but I could find no HKEX monthly-return or next-day-disclosure evidence of July/August 2026 repurchase activity, and the company's pattern is to announce capital returns with Q4 results in February, not with Q2. No evidence either way; not filed.

Hong Kong 9961.HK disclosures for anything the ADR tape has not seen — no dividend-consideration language in the 2026-09-02 board announcement (SEC ex-99.2 is a plain scheduling press release, not an HKEX board-meeting notice), and the 2026-06-30 filing is only the AGM results.

A September-dated company-specific surprise: no executive departure, no new regulatory action, no 6-K between 2026-09-02 and today. The co-founder resignations (Min Fan, Qi Ji) were 2026-02-25 and the Hagens Berman securities class action covers 30 Apr 2024 - 13 Jan 2026 — both old and priced.

The reporting-date drift (Q1 2025 reported ~19 May 2025 vs Q1 2026 on 24 Jun 2026; Q2 2025 on 1 Sep 2025 vs Q2 2026 on 15 Sep 2026). Genuinely odd and unexplained in any filing I could find, and H1 results on 16 Sep sits well past the two-month HKEX interim deadline, but I could not establish whether a waiver applies or find any market commentary on it. Unexplained, unsized, not filed.
Trip.com hiring pages, app-store review trend, and status/changelog pages — nothing retrievable that was both dated and interpretable inside the window.
baseline_tension: My net is mildly positive against a balanced skew (+0.61 vol points) that makes no directional statement, so there is no skew to contradict — but it does agree with the repo's free control (-run_up_20d_pct = +11.85%), which means it may add nothing over a number available before any hunting, and the +0.5 net is small enough that it should not be read as a call either way.
